source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.4.2 Queue Operations (PDF 101-102, printed 98-99). The printed code shows 'q.getO' and broken comment lines; a cleaned version is carried. MCQ 5, short question 5 and long question 5 are answered.

items: Enqueue: add an item at the back, like a person joining the end of the line.
Dequeue: remove the item at the front, like serving the first person.
Other operations: check whether the queue is empty, peek at the front item without removing it, and find the size.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
from queue import Queue    # built-in module
q = Queue()
q.put("Ahmed")    # enqueue
q.put("Fatima")
q.put("Ali")
print(q.queue[0])    # peek: Ahmed
print(q.get())       # dequeue: Ahmed
q.put("Sara")
print(list(q.queue)) # ['Fatima', 'Ali', 'Sara']

blocks.alt: Top left: five list items Decorations, Snacks, Cold drinks, Plates, Balloons with indexes 0 to 4 and notes on list operations. Top right: a stack of Book A, Book B and Book C with push adding at the top and pop removing Book C. Bottom left: a queue Ahmed, Fatima, Ali, Sara with dequeue at the front and enqueue at the back. Bottom right: stack states [3], [3, 4], [3, 4, 5], [3, 20], [23] while evaluating 3 4 5 * +.
blocks.caption: Lists, stacks, queues and postfix evaluation (original diagram after topics 4.1.1 to 4.1.5).
blocks.long_description: A list keeps items in order with indexes from 0, so Plates is at index 3, and items can be inserted, appended, removed or found. A stack of books is used only from the top: pushing adds Book C on top of Book B and Book A, and popping removes Book C first, the last one added. A queue serves from the front and adds at the back: Ahmed, who came first, is served first, and Sara joins behind Ali. To evaluate 3 4 5 * +, the numbers are pushed one by one; the * pops 5 and 4 and pushes 20, then + pops 20 and 3 and pushes the answer 23.

blocks.prompt: Which operation adds an item to a queue (MCQ 5)? Differentiate enqueue and dequeue (short question 5).
blocks.explanation: (c) Enqueue. Enqueue adds an item at the back (rear) of the queue; dequeue removes and returns the item at the front. Together they keep the first-in, first-out order.

blocks.prompt: Long question 5: write Python to simulate a queue of print jobs: create it, add three jobs, show the front job, remove it, add another and show the queue.
blocks.explanation: from queue import Queue; jobs = Queue(); jobs.put("Report.pdf"); jobs.put("Notes.docx"); jobs.put("Photo.png"); print("Front:", jobs.queue[0]); print("Printed:", jobs.get()); jobs.put("Slides.pptx"); print(list(jobs.queue)) shows Notes.docx, Photo.png, Slides.pptx. The file names are examples.

items: Queue in Python: Queue(); put() enqueues, get() dequeues, q.queue[0] peeks.
